proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
s_n:=\frac{n\log(d_n+1)}{d_n^2}=\frac{1}{r(n,d_n)}.
\tag{1}
\]
By Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}degree\mbox{-}growth}\), \(d_n^2/n\to0\), while Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}degree\mbox{-}lower}\) gives \(\log(d_n+1)\ge\log4>0\).  Hence (1) implies
\[
s_n=\frac{\log(d_n+1)}{d_n^2/n}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{2}
\]

We first prove the deterministic upper edge.  Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}retuned\mbox{-}seed\mbox{-}certificate\mbox{-}rate}\), applied under Assumptions~\(\mathrm{ass{:}degree\mbox{-}lower}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}degree\mbox{-}growth}\), supplies a constant \(C_{\mathrm{rob}}<\infty\), depending only on the once-fixed universal constant \(c_0\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), every simple \(d_n\)-regular graph \(G\) satisfies \(M_n<n\) and
\[
\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_n(G)}
\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_G,y}\!\left[
  (\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}-\tau_n)^2\mid G
\right]
\le C_{\mathrm{rob}}\frac{d_n^2}{n}.
\tag{3}
\]
Here \(\mathcal D_G\) is the selected seed assignment law in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}certified\mbox{-}procedure}\), and \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}\) is its observed-data estimator.  Conditional on the revealed \(G\), the schedule \(y\) is fixed and the seed assignment is the only randomness.  The same lemma proves that the assignment probabilities, Rao--Blackwell weights, and both candidate certificates are finite graph-measurable computations obtained by enumerating the ordered seed tuples.  Thus this pair is a feasible member of the infimum over \((\mathcal D_G,\widehat\tau)\) in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}minimax\mbox{-}risk}\).  Comparing that infimum with this feasible pair and using (3) gives
\[
R(G)
\le
\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_n(G)}
\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_G,y}\!\left[
  (\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}-\tau_n)^2\mid G
\right]
\le C_{\mathrm{rob}}\frac{d_n^2}{n}
\tag{4}
\]
for every such graph \(G\).  This establishes the first assertion with any universal \(C\ge C_{\mathrm{rob}}\); in particular, it uses no probability statement about \(G_n\).

We next prove the random-regular lower edge.  The regular-parity and uniform-regular-draw assumptions, together with the degree assumptions already used above, are precisely the random-environment hypotheses of Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}balanced\mbox{-}packing}\).  That theorem supplies a universal \(C_\beta<\infty\) for which
\[
E_n:=\{\beta(G_n)\le C_\beta s_n\}
\qquad\text{satisfies}\qquad
\Pr(E_n)\longrightarrow1.
\tag{5}
\]
On \(E_n\), Proposition~\(\mathrm{prop{:}balanced\mbox{-}bayes\mbox{-}converse}\) and (5) yield
\[
R(G_n)
\ge \frac{1}{12\{\beta(G_n)+2\}}
\ge \frac{1}{12(C_\beta s_n+2)}.
\tag{6}
\]
By (2), \(s_n\ge2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), and therefore
\[
C_\beta s_n+2\le(C_\beta+1)s_n.
\tag{7}
\]
Combining (1), (6), and (7), we obtain on \(E_n\)
\[
R(G_n)
\ge \frac{1}{12(C_\beta+1)s_n}
=\frac{1}{12(C_\beta+1)}
  \frac{d_n^2}{n\log(d_n+1)}.
\tag{8}
\]
The proposition is a lower bound on the minimax risk itself, so (8) holds after the infimum over every graph-dependent assignment law and measurable estimator; it does not merely lower-bound the risk of the seed procedure.  Taking
\[
c:=\{12(C_\beta+1)\}^{-1}>0,
\qquad
C:=\max\{C_{\mathrm{rob}},2c,1\}
\tag{9}
\]
gives \(0<c<C<\infty\), preserves (4), and, using (5), proves the second assertion.

For all sufficiently large \(n\), (4) holds for every graph in the support of the uniform simple regular law.  Hence the joint bracket event contains \(E_n\), and its probability tends to one by (5).  This proves the displayed corollary.

Finally suppose \(D:=\sup_n d_n<\infty\).  Assumption~\(\mathrm{ass{:}degree\mbox{-}lower}\) gives
\[
\frac{d_n^2}{\log(d_n+1)}\ge\frac{9}{\log(D+1)},
\qquad
d_n^2\le D^2.
\tag{10}
\]
Thus the joint bracket and (10) imply
\[
\Pr\!\left\{
\frac{9c}{\log(D+1)}\frac1n
\le R(G_n)\le
CD^2\frac1n
\right\}\longrightarrow1,
\tag{11}
\]
which is \(R(G_n)=\Theta_{\Pr}(n^{-1})\).  If instead \(d_n\to\infty\), the quotient of the displayed upper scale \(d_n^2/n\) by the displayed lower scale \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\) is exactly \(\log(d_n+1)\).  This establishes the stated elbow and records, rather than conceals, the remaining logarithmic gap.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
\textbf{Uniform upper edge and logarithmic random-regular bracket.}
There are universal constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) with the following properties for every admissible degree sequence.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For all sufficiently large \(n\) and every simple \(d_n\)-regular graph \(G\) on \(V_n\),
\[
R(G)\le C\frac{d_n^2}{n}.
\]
This deterministic upper edge is attained by the graph-measurable, one-shot selected seed procedure with its branch-safe all-treated fallback; its assignment law, estimator weights, and certificate are auditable by finite enumeration from \(G\).
\item Under the uniform simple random-regular draw,
\[
\Pr\!\left\{R(G_n)\ge c\frac{d_n^2}{n\log(d_n+1)}\right\}\longrightarrow1.
\]
This lower edge ranges over every graph-dependent assignment distribution and every measurable estimator.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently,
\[
\Pr\!\left\{
c\frac{d_n^2}{n\log(d_n+1)}
\le R(G_n)\le
C\frac{d_n^2}{n}
\right\}\longrightarrow1.
\]
If \((d_n)\) is bounded, then \(R(G_n)=\Theta_{\Pr}(n^{-1})\).  If \(d_n\to\infty\), the proved lower and upper edges differ by the factor \(\log(d_n+1)\); no matched order or unconditional logarithmic upper edge is asserted.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The active directive requires the stable theorem node to expose the strictly stronger quantifier already proved by its seed-certificate argument: the upper edge holds deterministically for every sufficiently large simple regular graph, whereas only the all-procedure lower edge is high probability. The split also states the bounded-degree elbow and labels the diverging-degree remainder as a logarithmic bracket, not a matched order.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The directive-authorized split claim explicitly names the revealed graph and its finite population, so the statement's symbol-invalidation metadata must add \(G\) and \(V_n\) while retaining the established proof spine.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: For every admissible degree sequence, a universal deterministic certified upper edge satisfies \(R(G)\le C d_n^2/n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\) and every simple \(d_n\)-regular \(G\), attained by the graph-auditable selected one-shot seed procedure. Under the uniform simple random-regular draw, \(\Pr\{R(G_n)\ge c d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\}\to1\), and the joint high-probability bracket follows. Bounded degree gives \(R(G_n)=\Theta_{\Pr}(n^{-1})\); when \(d_n\to\infty\), a factor \(\log(d_n+1)\) remains between the proved edges.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The functional must distinguish the deterministic every-graph upper edge from the random-regular lower event and must not advertise a matched frontier or an unconditional logarithmic upper edge.

prose_updates.tldr: For every admissible degree sequence and all sufficiently large \(n\), the graph-selected one-shot seed procedure gives the deterministic certified upper edge \(R(G)\le C d_n^2/n\) on every simple \(d_n\)-regular graph \(G\). Under the uniform simple random-regular draw, the balanced-exposure converse gives \(R(G_n)\ge c d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\) with probability tending to one, so the joint bracket is a corollary. Bounded degrees yield \(R(G_n)=\Theta_{\Pr}(n^{-1})\); diverging degrees leave a factor \(\log(d_n+1)\) between the proved edges. The selected procedure also gives finite conditional coverage and unconditional radius \(O(d_n/\sqrt{\alpha n})=o(1)\) for fixed \(\alpha\). A sharper logarithmic upper edge and radius remain conditional on the unresolved Boolean radius-two operator conjecture.

project_justification.gap: On the common uniform-simple-regular regime \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\), KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax gives the same \(d_n^2/n\) upper scale and a \(d_n/n\) lower scale for exactly the same two-endpoint outcome class and minimax functional. The present all-procedure lower edge is \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\), reducing the polynomial factor-\(d_n\) gap to a factor \(\log(d_n+1)\); equality with the lower edge remains open.
project_justification.fill: The note proves a deterministic certified upper edge on every sufficiently large simple regular graph by inserting the robust candidate into the exact selected seed/Schur certificate and then using that procedure as a feasible competitor in the minimax infimum. Separately, balanced simultaneous endpoint exposure and the Bayes converse give the random-regular lower edge over every design and estimator. Their conjunction yields the high-probability logarithmic bracket, while exact seed-tuple enumeration supplies a finite graph audit and the risk certificate yields the stated design-based confidence guarantee. The Boolean operator conjecture is retained only as a conditional refinement.

prose_updates.related_work: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, arXiv:2608.04909v1, Corollary 5.4 and Appendix E.4, is the closest comparator. On the common uniform-simple-regular regime \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\), its \(q=2\) GATE outcome class and minimax functional coincide exactly with this note's \(\mathcal M_n(G)\) and \(R(G)\); this is equality of the compared problem, not a class-inclusion transfer. It places that risk between \(d_n/n\) and \(d_n^2/n\). The present balanced-exposure converse improves the lower edge to \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\), while the selected seed certificate provides a deterministic, graph-auditable upper edge at the same \(d_n^2/n\) order, leaving a logarithmic gap. Its Algorithm 4 and Proposition 4.3 motivate finite design computation but do not give this selected seed certificate. KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph, arXiv:2411.10908v3, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 4.1, supplies a generic conflict-graph variance scale; the current unconditional upper edge does not strictly improve that scale. UganderYin2023RGCR studies randomized graph cluster designs under bounded outcomes and a fixed Horvitz--Thompson procedure, rather than unrestricted minimax risk. AronowSamii2017GeneralInterference supplies the exposure-mapping foundation. BehagueIlkovicMontgomery2025Sandwich supports the proved random-regular packing transfer in its verified degree regime. Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices, CCC 2025 Theorems 14--15, treats graph-matrix shapes but does not uniformly resum the unbounded \(K_{2,r}\)-type terms in the Boolean inclusion--exclusion expansion. BauerschmidtEtAl2020EdgeRigidity and Sarid2023SpectralGap control adjacency spectra, not this Boolean correction. HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance optimizes conservative bounds for fixed linear estimators and does not choose the minimax design. ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice remains the prospective application: a larger one-round all-free versus all-fixed random-regular public-goods experiment can use the robust certificate without assuming its behavioral outcomes attain worst-case risk.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The established result consists of a deterministic certified upper edge and a random-regular lower edge, with their joint logarithmic bracket as a corollary; it is not a matched frontier. For every admissible sequence, the selected robust seed candidate gives \(R(G)\le C d_n^2/n\) on every sufficiently large simple \(d_n\)-regular graph. The balanced-packing argument gives \(R(G_n)\ge c d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\) with high probability over the uniform graph and uniformly over all procedures. Thus bounded degree has order \(n^{-1}\), while diverging degree retains a logarithmic gap. The Boolean operator estimate remains an explicit conjecture and yields only a conditional sharper edge. Seed probabilities and inverse weights are formed only on \(M_n<n\); the complementary branch uses an all-treated fallback. The result concerns one assignment, unrestricted intermediate ANI outcomes, and the full population GATE. It does not cover later strategic feedback, final wealth, two-hop individual payoff, repeated experiments, nonuniform graph draws, or a claim that the ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice behavioral model is worst case.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem separates a deterministic certified upper edge, attained by an explicit graph-auditable one-shot design, from a random-regular all-procedure lower edge; together they reduce the former polynomial gap to a logarithmic bracket.
statement_notes.gap: For exactly the common \(q=2\) GATE outcome class and minimax functional, KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax has the same \(d_n^2/n\) upper scale but only a \(d_n/n\) lower scale. Matching the new \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\) lower edge, or proving the conditional logarithmic upper refinement, remains open.
statement_notes.consumer: ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice motivates using the deterministic error certificate and the honest logarithmic bracket, rather than a point rate, to size a larger one-round all-free versus all-fixed random-regular experiment and to expose the bounded-degree \(n^{-1}\) elbow.
